entities.summary:
Muirchertach Ua Briain, son of Toirdelbach Ua Briain and great-grandson of Brian Boru, was King of Munster and later self-declared High King of Ireland.

Born around 1040, Muirchertach Ua Briain rose to prominence in the late 11th century, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various Irish kingdoms.

He seized the opportunity to unite the various Irish kingdoms under his rule, establishing a loose confederation of kingdoms that would last for several decades.

Muirchertach Ua Briain's reign marked a turning point in Irish history, as he successfully resisted the attempts of the Norman invaders to conquer Ireland.

He died on March 10, 1119, and was succeeded by his son, Cormac Ua Briain, who would go on to continue his father's legacy.

Muirchertach Ua Briain's legacy extended beyond Ireland's borders, as he played a significant role in shaping the course of European history during the High Middle Ages.

In the annals of Irish history, Muirchertach Ua Briain's name stands as a testament to the enduring spirit of Irish resistance and determination.

A great leader, Muirchertach Ua Briain remains an important figure in the annals of Irish history, his bravery and strategic vision leaving a lasting impact on the course of Irish civilization.
